assumptions.text: The installed Vibe 3.1.4 headless flag surface (model alias selection, thinking level, approval policy, custom agents, tool enable/disable lists, prompt and system-prompt files, budget guards, and structured exit evidence) is sufficient to serve every backend request type the current session transport serves, so a shared plain-CLI adapter can replace it.

A custom policy or agent can authorize exactly the insrc analysis tools while leaving every other tool blocked, without a blanket approval bypass — unproven, which is why the Epic carries a fail-closed qualification gate rather than assuming success.
The plugin chat's streaming UX, resume handles and attachments survive being routed through the shared adapter unchanged in behavior.
The chat prompt-transport defect recorded in the ledger is already fixed by the current explicit prompt binding and needs verification and closure, not rework.
A real TOML parser is already a project dependency and its parse covers the grammar needs of all three hand-written Vibe config readers, so adoption is a replacement, not new machinery.

constraints.text: Read-only analysis authorization ships only on successful live qualification that proves every non-allowed tool stays blocked without a blanket permission bypass; on failure the session fails closed and analysis stays unavailable.
One shared plain-CLI execution adapter serves both the backend provider and the plugin chat; the session-based transport is not retained in any form — not as a fallback, not as a verification layer.
Model, effort, prompt transport, safety handling and the exact MCP tool naming are qualified against the installed CLI and aligned by construction across both surfaces.

Vibe configuration files are parsed with a real TOML parser for understanding, and edits are surgical: unrelated user settings survive registration and cleanup byte-for-byte; a config that cannot be changed safely is left untouched with the failure reported.
Review integration is out of scope until the review rewrite establishes its replacement; the review-dependent issues are recorded as deferred dependencies on it, not closed.
All model work happens through the locally-installed CLI binary's own session (auth, quota, subprocess); no direct cloud REST is introduced.
Issues close only with supporting evidence; no speculative closures.

openQuestions: Item a2: the low-confidence assumption that a custom policy or agent can authorize exactly the insrc analysis tools without a blanket bypass has no open-question record (the s2 schema carries none); it is carried structurally by constraint k1 and the s2 qualification story — the design stage should confirm the fail-closed gate is the agreed resolution or raise the question explicitly.
body.problem: Mistral Vibe is wired into the system through three mechanisms that disagree with each other. Backend model requests take one path for the default model but switch to a separate session-based transport whenever a model or thinking level is chosen — a split that no longer reflects the installed tool's capabilities — while the VS Code chat launches the same tool a third way and pins models through an environment variable. The mechanisms disagree on safety: a read-only session can read files but cannot call the insrc analysis tools at all, because the tool allowlist it relies on does not govern the tool's separate approval gate, so the sessions cannot do the analysis work they exist for. They disagree on tool naming, with the backend and the plugin assuming two different spellings for the same tools. Configuration files are read through hand-written approximations of TOML that have repeatedly misread valid user settings — most recently forcing nine rounds of validation hardening on a single cleanup function — and the integration's issue ledger has drifted: one record appears fixed by other work, and two more are predicated on review machinery that has since been removed from the codebase. The net effect is an integration that is over-complex where the claude and codex clients need one mechanism, unsafe where it matters most, and untrustworthy in its configuration handling and its own records.

summary.prose: This Epic makes Mistral Vibe a fully-supported model client, equal to the claude and codex clients: one launch path serves both the backend and the VS Code chat, model selection works through the tool's own supported interface, and the redundant session machinery goes away. Read-only sessions either gain the ability to run insrc's analysis tools with everything else provably blocked, or honestly report that analysis is unavailable — they never trade safety for capability. Configuration files are read with a real parser so users' unrelated settings survive every edit, the tool naming is established once against the installed tool, and the issue ledger is brought back in line with reality: what is fixed is closed, what is deferred says so.
